1. In this revision, the revisionist/complainant (hereinafter referred to as complainant) has challenged the order of Ld. Trial Court dated 17.02.2024, whereby the after considering the statements of the complainant/CW1 and her son/CW2, the Ld. Trial Court found that there was not sufficient ground to summon the respondents for further proceedings and dismissed the complaint.

2. Necessary facts for deciding the revision are that in May 2015, the respondents approached the complainant and offered to sell her a flat bearing no. J-1003, Amrapali Platinum, Sector-119, Noida,
UP, representing themselves as the joint owners of the said flat.
The complainant agreed to purchase the said flat for a sum of Rs. 40 lac and paid Rs. 25 lac by cheque and Rs. 5 lac in cash as the earnest money.
The respondents assured that the possession thereof would be handed over to the complainant within 6 months after finding a suitable accommodation for themselves.
The respondents had also acknowledged the earnest money received from the complainant.
The respondents had executed a Receipt cum Sale agreement and had also given the original flat buyer agreement, allotment letter and payment receipts to the complainant.
After six months, when the complainant asked the Digitally respondents to handover the possession of the flat, the signed by SUBHASH SUBHASH KUMAR respondents sought some more time in this regard.

When the complainant informed the aforesaid fact to the respondents, they requested the complainant not to lodge an FIR and assured that they would repay her the entire amount along with Rs. 6 lac as damages within six months.
They also gave two cheques of Rs. 30 lac and of Rs. 6 lac to the complainant.
However, the said cheques were dishonoured on being presented for encashment.

3. The complainant approached the concerned police station for lodging the FIR but the police did not lodge the FIR and therefore, the complainant had filed an application under Section 156(3)
Cr.P.C. before the Ld. Trial Court seeking direction to the concerned SHO for lodging the FIR,
however, vide its order dated 03.03.2022, the said application was dismissed by the Ld. Trial Court and the complainant was directed to lead pre- summoning evidence.
4. Complainant examined herself as CW1 and her son namely Prashant Kumar as CW2.

However,
the said complaint was dismissed vide the impugned order.
Hence, this revision.

In the impugned order, the Ld. Trial Court has observed as under:
"The complainant has premised the allegations of cheating and forgery on the basis that the accused persons failed to deliver the property and to refund the amount paid.
However, this only shows the subsequent conduct of the accused persons after the complainant gave the amount.
As per the record, the complainant Digitally signed by SUBHASH granted time to the accused persons to refund the amount lateron.

SUBHASH KUMAR KUMAR MISHRA MISHRA Date: The facts, therefore, doesn't not show that accused persons had 2025.03.12 15:29:21 +0530 Shakuntala Singh Vs.

sentences.text: Moreover, the complainant could not bring any evidence to show that the payment receipt issued by the accused persons were forged and fabricated one.
The matter seems to be a case of non delivery of property and of civil nature.
Therefore, I am of view that no case is made out against any accused for cheating and forgery."
(emphasis given)

11. Ld. Trial Court has observed in the impugned order that from the facts, it appear that the respondents had no intention to cheat or deceive the complainant since beginning and that the complainant did not adduce evidence to show that the payment receipts were forged.

12. As per law laid down in Nagawwa (supra), where the allegations made in the complaint, or the statements of the witnesses recorded in support of the same taken at their face value make out prima facie case against the accused or the complaint discloses the essential ingredients of an offence, which is alleged against the accused, the accused can be summoned.

It means that at the stage of summoning only the allegations made in the complaint and the statements of the witnesses, are to be taken at their face value and the accused can not be summoned only if after considering it, no case is made out against him.
SUBHASH KUMAR MISHRA 13.

Further, at the stage of pre-summoning evidence, the Date: 2025.03.12 Shakuntala Singh Vs.
Madhu Kumari & Anr. Page no.6 of 8 complainant is not required to prove his case by adducing irrefutable evidence.

In the instant case, in her evidence, the complainant/CW1 has produced and exhibited the alleged forged payment receipt of Rs. 43 lac as Ex.CW1/5.
14.

Therefore, from the complaint and the testimonies of CW1 and CW2, it was prima facie shown by the complainant that the receipt Ex.CW1/5 had been forged by the respondents and it was handed over to the complainant, when the agreement to sale was executed.

15. Therefore, from allegations in the complainant and from the testimonies of the witnesses, it prima facie appears that the respondents intended to cheat the complainant since inception of the transaction and therefore, there was prima facie material available on the record to summon the respondents.

The matter is remanded back to Ld. KUMAR MISHRA trial court to proceed with the matter in accordance with law.
